prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (policy-focused, up to 500 words)

- Economy and tax: Responsible fiscal rules; repair EU trade; industrial strategy for green, digital and bioscience sectors; HMRC resourcing; priority future income tax cut via higher personal allowance; reverse bank tax cuts; 6% Digital Services Tax; fairer capital gains; 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks; expand British Business Bank; financial inclusion strategy.

- Business and jobs: Replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; skills and training levy to replace apprenticeship levy; target 3% of GDP R&D by 2030; AI cross-sector regulation; prompt payment enforcement; scale-up finance outside SE; employee ownership rights.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% electricity from renewables by 2030; 10-year home energy upgrades with free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households; social energy tariff; decouple power prices from gas; end fossil fuel subsidies; no fracking/new coal; expand storage, interconnectors and community energy; rooftop solar incentives.

- Health (NHS): Right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours urgent) with 8,000 more GPs; universal 24/7 booking; expand pharmacy roles; NHS dentist access for urgent care; mental health hubs for youth and regular check-ups; 100% cancer treatment start within 62 days; 10-year estates plan; digital interoperability; faster access to new medicines via EU mutual recognition.

- Social care: Free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers and a Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); cross-party funding commission; unpaid carers: paid leave and guaranteed respite; independent living taskforce; portability of care packages.

- Education and skills: Mental health professional in every school; per-pupil funding above inflation; national repairs programme; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; Early Years pupil premium tripled; maintenance grants restored; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000); SEND national body; broaden curriculum; strengthened careers/technical routes.

- Families and children: Free school meals for all children in poverty; day-one parental rights incl. self-employed; maternity/shared pay to £350/week; paternity at 90% pay plus extra month for partners; Erasmus Plus return; “Toddler Top-Up.”

- Welfare and pensions: Remove two-child limit and benefit cap; target ending deep poverty; triple lock protected; fair compensation for 1950s-born women; reduce UC wait to five days; scrap bedroom tax; reform sanctions; increase and widen Carer’s Allowance.

- Crime and justice: Community policing; guarantee all burglaries attended; invest to cut court backlogs; Online Crime Agency; end disproportionate stop and search; strengthen fraud reimbursement; youth diversion duty; expand restorative justice; prison rehabilitation and women’s justice reforms.

- Natural environment: Transform water companies into public benefit companies; tougher regulator; sewage tax; real-time discharge data; binding ‘double nature by 2050’ targets; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single-use plastics; protect 30% land/sea by 2030.

- Food and farming: National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund ELMs (+£1bn/yr); maintain standards in trade; UK‑EU veterinary and plant health agreements; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; animal welfare bill (incl. ban caged hens); antimicrobials controls.

- Housing: 380,000 homes/year (150,000 social); 10 garden cities; neighbourhood planning; reform land compensation; brownfield first with affordable quotas; “use-it-or-lose-it” permissions; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; end Section 21 and create 3‑year default tenancies; landlord register; rent-to-own; remove dangerous cladding; end rough sleeping.

- Local government and communities: Multi-year settlements; powers over second homes/short lets; gigabit broadband nationwide; rural fuel relief; local planning fees; protect community assets.

- Transport: EV transition (charge points, grid upgrades, card access, 5% VAT on public charging, plug-in grant, 2030 ZEV sales); freeze rail fares and simplify tickets; rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail, accessibility; bus franchising and £2 fare cap; active travel networks; shift more roads budget to maintenance; aviation taxes focused on frequent flyers; private jet super tax; restrict short domestic flights with fast rail alternatives.

- Culture, media and sport: Protect BBC/S4C/Channel 4; Creative Europe and artist mobility with EU; Anti‑SLAPP law; problem gambling levy and affordability checks; independent football regulator; grassroots sport investment.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work and student visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; safe/legal routes; 3‑month asylum decision standard; allow work after 3 months; flexible, sector‑based work visas; expand Youth Mobility; reverse family visa threshold rise; secure Settled Status evidence; implement Windrush Review.

- Rights and equality: Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; make misogyny a hate crime; ban conversion practices; restore protest protections; Digital Bill of Rights; stronger disability rights (UNCRPD, Access to Work reform, adjustment passports); assisted dying free vote.

- Political reform and devolution: Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; cap donations; Ministerial Code in law; Lords reform; citizens’ assemblies; transparency on ministerial communications; federal approach and stronger devolved powers.

- Defence: Increase defence spending toward 2.5% GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; arms export presumption of denial to HR concerns; procurement reform; improve housing and support for personnel and veterans; deepen European and NATO cooperation.

- International: Restore 0.7% ODA with poverty focus; phased EU rapprochement (agencies/programmes, SPS/MRAs, Single Market goal long-term); support Ukraine (including seizing frozen Russian assets); Israel-Gaza immediate ceasefire and two-state solution; proscribe IRGC; BBC World Service funding; global human rights sanctions and advocacy.
